newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer, USD/yen in the driving seat.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer, USD/yen in the driving seat.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar, driven more by the dollar's demise against the yen than local fundamentals, ended Wednesday higher, partly rectifying easier monetary conditions seen overnight.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6945/52, up from 0.6935/40 at the opening, having hit a high of 0.6955 during the session. On its Trade-Weighted Index, the currency ended at 67.17 from 67.04.
Dealers said dollar/yen remained firmly in the driver's seat, especially given the yen's vital weighting on the TWI.
The Monetary Conditions Index was minus 86 basis points, having sunk lower overnight when the Fed decided to leave rates unchanged.
"I guess it's been a fairly major move in terms of what the Fed didn't do, and the implications for New Zealand on the MCI and the TWI," he said.
"It's the dollar/yen that is holding the key for us at the moment and the Kiwi is just hanging in there," he said.
That said, traders were reluctant to take Kiwi up or down.

"The economy is performing poorly and I suppose that is what is making it hard to convince people to get long Kiwi at these levels as it's really been the dollar/yen move that's seen the Kiwi get to where it is," another dealer said, adding, "If there were any correction there, we would expect weakness in the Kiwi in line with the general economy."
Meanwhile the dollar was showing no signs of recovering against the yen, ending locally at 113.90-00 -- a slight improvement on New York's close.
Expected overnight range for the Kiwi -- US$0.6930-60.
